claim: In Arabidopsis, genetic defects in DCL1/CARPEL FACTORY and HEN1 connect developmental phenotypes to reduced or altered miRNA accumulation, but the two genes represent distinguishable pathway functions rather than a single undifferentiated 'miRNA defect'.

experimental_context.tissue: whole-plant and floral tissues in mutant analyses
experimental_context.genotype: carpel factory/dcl1 and hen1 mutant alleles

limitations: The 2002 work predates current miRNA annotation and pathway vocabulary.
Developmental pleiotropy does not by itself localize a defect to transcription, processing, stabilization or action.

claim: For tested Arabidopsis targets, AMP1 and ER-associated membrane-bound polysomes are required for miRNA-mediated translational repression but not for the cleavage arm, demonstrating that target action must be decomposed by mode and subcellular context.

experimental_context.tissue: Arabidopsis tissues used for microsome and polysome assays

limitations: Subcellular localization and mode-of-action claims are based on a defined Arabidopsis system.
The official lecture report is contextual only and does not replace the primary paper.

supporting_location.section: abstract and membrane-bound polysome analyses; official lecture report

claim: The official academic Q&A describes a research trajectory in which floral-patterning genetic screens uncovered RNA-related genes and redirected the program toward miRNAs and other small RNAs; this supports a genetics-led discovery history, not a mechanistic claim by itself.

experimental_context.tissue: flowers and whole plants in historical research program

limitations: Institutional Q&A is appropriate for trajectory and scope, not independent validation of molecular facts.
The lecture announcement has no transcript and supports title/scope only.

claim: Purified Arabidopsis HEN1 preferentially methylates 21-24-nt small-RNA duplexes with short 3' overhangs and places the methyl group on the 2'-OH of the 3'-terminal nucleotide, so substrate architecture is part of mechanistic interpretation.

experimental_context.treatment: in vitro methyltransferase reactions with substrate panels

limitations: In vitro preference is not an absolute in vivo classification rule.
Do not transfer the measured Arabidopsis enzyme specificity automatically to animal HEN1 homologs.

claim: Arabidopsis HEN1 catalyzes methylation of plant small-RNA duplex products at the terminal ribose, establishing terminal modification as a biochemical stage of plant miRNA and siRNA metabolism.

experimental_context.genotype: wild type and hen1 mutants; purified HEN1 in vitro

limitations: These studies establish Arabidopsis HEN1 biochemistry; homolog behavior in other taxa requires organism-specific evidence.
Methylation status does not establish a small RNA's biological target or phenotype.

claim: HESO1 is a terminal nucleotidyltransferase that uridylates unmethylated miRNAs and siRNAs in Arabidopsis hen1 backgrounds, and genetic suppression links that tailing activity to altered small-RNA stability and phenotypes.

experimental_context.genotype: hen1-1 or hen1-2 with heso1 suppressor alleles

limitations: Primary evidence is centered on unmethylated substrates in hen1 mutant backgrounds.
Chen is a middle coauthor; this is a team result rather than an individually authored position.

claim: In Arabidopsis hen1 mutants, loss of terminal methylation exposes miRNAs and several siRNA classes to 3'-end uridylation and altered size profiles, supporting a protective role for methylation at small-RNA 3' ends.

experimental_context.genotype: hen1 mutant alleles versus wild type

limitations: The mutant context reveals vulnerability of unmethylated small RNAs; it does not quantify turnover of every wild-type small RNA.
miRNAs and siRNAs remain distinct classes even when both are HEN1 substrates.

claim: In Arabidopsis flower development, miR172 regulates APETALA2 primarily through translational repression in the tested system, supported by target-site perturbation and protein-versus-RNA measurements rather than sequence complementarity alone.

experimental_context.tissue: flowers
experimental_context.genotype: wild type and transgenic miR172/AP2 target-site contexts

limitations: This is a specific miR172-AP2 result and must not be generalized to all plant miRNA-target pairs.
Target regulation and floral phenotype causality require the tested genetic context; prediction alone would be insufficient.

claim: In the tested Arabidopsis mobile-miRNA system, microtubules promote non-cell-autonomous action by limiting cytoplasmic AGO1 loading, distinguishing cytoplasmic loading of mobile miRNAs from nuclear loading associated with cell-autonomous action.

experimental_context.tissue: root cell layers and cell-type-specific contexts
experimental_context.genotype: cell-type-specific AGO1 and microtubule perturbation contexts

limitations: Do not generalize to all plant miRNAs, tissues or long-distance transport.
Detection in another cell is not by itself proof of loading, target engagement or phenotype causality.

claim: Arabidopsis RBV affects both miRNA biogenesis and AGO1 loading, so a changed mature-miRNA level can reflect multiple checkpoints and should be resolved with processing, splicing and loading assays rather than abundance alone.
limitations: RBV's effects do not imply that all biogenesis factors also directly regulate AGO1 loading.
Shared corresponding authorship means the finding belongs to a multi-institution team.

claim: Arabidopsis SMALL RNA DEGRADING NUCLEASE family activity can degrade mature miRNAs, and perturbing multiple SDN genes changes miRNA abundance and development, linking mature-miRNA turnover to phenotype.
limitations: A formal erratum exists; figure-level or quantitative reuse requires consultation of the correction details.
Pleiotropic developmental phenotypes do not identify a single miRNA as the only causal substrate.

claim: A useful Chen-derived diagnostic lens is to separate MIR transcription, DCL1-associated processing, HEN1-dependent stabilization, AGO loading, target cleavage or translational repression, and mature-miRNA turnover before assigning a single cause to altered small-RNA abundance or phenotype.
limitations: This staged diagnostic is an agent synthesis of repeated public research framing, not a verbatim expert rule.
Later work can subdivide or revise individual stages; the review sources have 2005 and 2013 cutoffs.

supporting_location.section: review pathway organization; official lecture abstract

claim: In the tested Arabidopsis hen1-2 suppressor context, reducing Pol IV/RDR2-dependent 24-nt siRNA production can restore miRNA methylation, showing that pathway interpretation may require considering competition among HEN1 substrate pools.

experimental_context.genotype: hen1-2 with Pol IV- or RDR2-pathway suppressor mutations

limitations: The inference is allele- and pathway-context dependent.
It does not imply that all miRNA level changes are caused by substrate competition.

claim: Public academic materials repeatedly frame plant-miRNA questions in terms of both pathway step ('how') and subcellular location ('where'), including nuclear pore, ER and membrane-bound-polysome contexts.
limitations: The event materials are abstracts/reports, not transcripts, and cannot establish wording style or Q&A behavior.
Detailed mechanistic claims require the cited primary paper or other direct evidence.

claim: A recurring Chen-linked analysis decomposes plant miRNA abundance into transcription, pri-miRNA processing/stability, duplex methylation, AGO loading, localization or movement, target action, and turnover before assigning mechanism.
limitations: The full lifecycle decomposition is synthesized across publications rather than stated as a named checklist in one paper.
Some stages are supported in different Arabidopsis tissues and mutant backgrounds and must not be collapsed into a single experiment.
The AAR2 contribution must travel with its correction version chain; the correction is contextual provenance and not independent scientific support.

supporting_location.page_or_figure: PMC article figures and model diagrams

claim: Mechanistic diagnosis should preserve RNA-entity resolution: MIR transcription and pri-miRNA abundance do not by themselves report pre-miRNA end precision, mature-duplex production, terminal methylation, or AGO-loaded mature miRNA.
limitations: The 2019 pre-miRNA paper is used only to the level stated in its abstract in this research pass.
The exact detectable intermediate varies by MIR locus and assay.

supporting_location.page_or_figure: pre-miRNA 3' end analysis; HEN1 substrate assays; AGO1-IP analyses

claim: In the Arabidopsis miR172-APETALA2 case, target-site and protein-level evidence separate direct post-transcriptional regulation from downstream floral phenotype; transcript abundance alone would miss the reported translational-repression mechanism.

experimental_context.tissue: flowers
experimental_context.genotype: wild type and miR172/APETALA2 transgenic or target-site-altered material

limitations: This is a specific Arabidopsis miR172/APETALA2 example, not proof that translational repression dominates every plant miRNA-target pair.
Target directness and whole-flower phenotype causality remain distinct axes.

supporting_location.page_or_figure: target-site transgenes, RNA and protein comparisons

claim: HEN1-mediated 2'-O-methylation of plant miRNA/miRNA-star duplex products protects small RNAs from 3'-end tailing and trimming; methylation state and end heterogeneity therefore diagnose a stability step rather than transcription or DCL1 cleavage alone.

experimental_context.tissue: whole seedlings/plant tissues used in cited studies

limitations: HEN1 has multiple small-RNA substrates; developmental phenotypes cannot be assigned to one miRNA without additional evidence.
End-modification behavior depends on AGO association and substrate context.

supporting_location.page_or_figure: beta-elimination/mass analysis and small-RNA end profiles

claim: Recombinant HEN1 substrate tests locate the modification step by showing preference for 21-24-nt duplex substrates and methyl deposition on the 2' hydroxyl of the 3' terminal nucleotide; steady-state mature-miRNA loss alone would not establish this biochemical step.
limitations: In vitro substrate preference does not alone quantify in vivo competition among endogenous small-RNA classes.
The tested Arabidopsis enzyme and substrates do not authorize unqualified transfer to animals.

claim: Suppressor genetics and epistasis can disaggregate pleiotropic small-RNA-mutant phenotypes: reducing Pol IV-dependent siRNA production restores miRNA methylation in a partial hen1 background, supporting competition for limiting HEN1 rather than a single downstream developmental pathway.

experimental_context.tissue: seedlings/plant tissues
experimental_context.genotype: hen1-2 and second-site Pol IV-pathway suppressors

limitations: The competition model is established in a partial hen1 allele and should not be generalized to every HEN1 dosage or tissue.
Phenotypic rescue is not equivalent to full biochemical restoration of all small-RNA classes.

supporting_location.page_or_figure: suppressor mapping, methylation and small-RNA measurements

claim: Total miRNA abundance and AGO1 loading are separable observables: RBV perturbation changes miRNA biogenesis and the fraction loaded into AGO1, so a loading mechanism requires AGO1-associated measurements rather than total small-RNA sequencing alone.

experimental_context.tissue: Arabidopsis seedlings

limitations: RBV may affect more than one lifecycle stage; AGO1-IP enrichment must be interpreted with total-input and protein controls.
The tested Arabidopsis factor does not establish a universal loading factor in all plants.

claim: Subcellular localization supports mechanism only when paired with perturbation and molecular readouts: TREX-2/nuclear-pore studies combine localization or interaction evidence with genetics, processing, AGO1 loading and export measurements rather than treating colocalization as causality.

experimental_context.tissue: Arabidopsis tissues and protoplast/cellular assays used in study

limitations: A physical link between stages does not mean a factor has identical effects on processing, loading and export.
Localization patterns can be assay- and construct-dependent.

supporting_location.page_or_figure: interaction/localization plus mutant RNA and export assays

claim: For mobile Arabidopsis miR165/166, source-cell AGO1 loading and intercellular movement are competing fates in the tested context: KTN1-dependent microtubule behavior inhibits cytoplasmic loading in source cells, enabling non-cell-autonomous action.

experimental_context.tissue: source and recipient root cell layers

limitations: The result is bounded to tested miR165/166 source/recipient tissues and does not establish that all plant miRNAs move by this rule.
Movement, AGO1 loading, target repression and developmental phenotype require distinct readouts.

supporting_location.page_or_figure: cell-type perturbations, movement reporters and AGO1-loading assays

claim: Small-RNA 3' end states are conditioned by AGO1 association, methylation and substrate identity; tailing or truncation profiles should therefore be interpreted jointly with AGO occupancy and not as a standalone measure of biogenesis failure.
limitations: Cross-species conservation is pattern-level and does not imply identical modification frequency for homologous miRNA families.
AGO1 dependence may differ among individual miRNAs and tissues.

claim: Normal MIR promoter activity together with accelerated pri-miRNA decay in aar2 mutants localizes the defect downstream of transcription and upstream of mature-miRNA accumulation; paired promoter and RNA-decay assays are needed to make that distinction.

experimental_context.tissue: Arabidopsis seedlings/tissues used in study

limitations: AAR2 is also a splicing factor, so indirect effects and pleiotropy remain relevant even with stage-localizing assays.

The verified correction affects Fig. 1 and Fig. S3 legends and Figs. 6, S2, and S6. The promoter result used here is in Fig. 3 and the pri-miRNA decay result is in Fig. 4, so this claim does not depend on an affected panel; affected-panel reuse still requires the corrected online version.

supporting_location.page_or_figure: Original corrected online article: Fig. 3 (MIR promoter reporters) and Fig. 4 (pri-miRNA decay); correction affects Fig. 1/Fig. S3 legends and Figs. 6/S2/S6

claim: Across Chen-linked studies, a reusable decision rule is to triangulate genetics with a stage-specific biochemical or localization assay and an RNA-species-resolved measurement, while treating phenotype rescue as downstream corroboration rather than sufficient mechanistic proof.

entities.precursor: pri-miRNA, pre-miRNA or duplex as appropriate
entities.mature_arm: mature or AGO-loaded miRNA as appropriate

limitations: This is an agent-derived synthesis, not a quotation or named framework authored by Xuemei Chen.
The recurrence is strong across several contexts, but distinctiveness from other rigorous plant small-RNA laboratories must be judged at N1.5/N2.5.
A study may legitimately use different assay combinations when the lifecycle stage or biological question differs.

claim: The 2002 Chen-team genetics established that DCL1/CARPEL FACTORY and HEN1 are required for normal Arabidopsis miRNA accumulation and development, but those pleiotropic phenotypes did not by themselves assign every defect to transcription, processing, loading, action, or turnover.

experimental_context.tissue: whole aerial tissues/developmental material as reported
experimental_context.genotype: carpel factory/dcl1 and hen1 mutant contexts

limitations: A genetic requirement is not a complete biochemical step assignment.
Broad developmental phenotypes can be secondary to multiple miRNA defects.

claim: The miR172/APETALA2 study made protein-level measurement central to a plant miRNA developmental mechanism, and later independent work supports translational repression as a genuine plant miRNA action mode distinct from slicing.

experimental_context.tissue: flowers and plant-cell biochemical system

limitations: The relative contribution of cleavage, RNA decay, and translation repression is target- and context-specific.
A protein/RNA mismatch in one target cannot be generalized to every miRNA target.

claim: HEN1-mediated terminal methylation is a protective step for plant small RNAs, with independent enzyme kinetics supporting preferential and efficient modification of duplex RNA while showing that the full protein contributes to substrate interaction.

experimental_context.genotype: wild type and hen1 contexts; purified enzyme

limitations: Purified-enzyme kinetics do not measure in-vivo substrate access or turnover.
Methylation status alone does not identify the downstream nuclease or terminal transferase.

claim: Loss of HEN1-dependent methylation exposes Arabidopsis miRNAs and siRNAs to 3′ uridylation, but the observed tail is evidence of altered end metabolism rather than proof of a single linear degradation enzyme or rate-limiting step.

experimental_context.tissue: whole-plant small RNA

limitations: Steady-state tail frequencies are not degradation-rate measurements.
HESO1 and URT1 show redundancy and substrate/context differences.

claim: Independent genetics and cell-biological work support SERRATE as part of the DCL1–HYL1 plant pri-miRNA processing machinery, while its roles in splicing and phase-separated D-bodies warn against treating visible localization or mutant phenotype as a locus-specific processing-rate measurement.

experimental_context.tissue: Arabidopsis seedlings/cells
experimental_context.genotype: se, cbp80/abh1, cbp20 and phase-separation perturbations

limitations: SERRATE and CBC perturbations also alter splicing.
D-body abundance is not automatically equal to processing flux for every MIR locus.

claim: Independent HYL1 structural, interaction, and rescue experiments support direct dsRNA binding and a dimerization-based contribution to miRNA precursor processing, but the structural model remains narrower than the complete in-vivo DCL1 cleavage cycle.

experimental_context.tissue: transgenic Arabidopsis and purified components

limitations: Domain swapping/rescue does not prove every precursor uses identical geometry.
Protein interaction and binding do not alone quantify processing accuracy in each tissue.

claim: Plant miRNA-guided translational inhibition is genetically separable from endonucleolytic cleavage and can be reproduced with AGO1-RISC in a biochemical translation system, so RNA-only target assays are insufficient to exclude direct regulation.

experimental_context.tissue: Arabidopsis genetic reporters and plant-cell lysate

limitations: Biochemical reconstitution does not establish in-vivo prevalence.
Protein reduction can also be indirect unless sequence-specific miRNA/target dependence is demonstrated.

claim: Arabidopsis small-RNA 3′ turnover is a branched network in which HESO1 and URT1 can act synergistically or redundantly and reduced uridylation can expose trimming; URT1 structure supports a distinct catalytic basis but not in-vivo flux by itself.

experimental_context.tissue: whole-plant small RNA and purified URT1

limitations: The genetic paper includes Xuemei Chen and is not independent.
An enzyme structure does not show which endogenous miRNAs dominate its in-vivo substrate pool.

claim: Independent cell-type and HASTY studies support spatial regulation and movement of Arabidopsis miRNAs, but production in a source cell, movement, recipient AGO loading, target repression, and phenotype are distinct evidentiary gates.

experimental_context.tissue: root tip, cell-to-cell and vascular contexts

limitations: These papers share the Voinnet collaboration cluster and count as one independent group.
Reporter movement does not automatically establish movement of every endogenous family member.

claim: Chen-team work supports a model in which cortical microtubules promote non-cell-autonomous miRNA action by limiting cytoplasmic AGO1 loading, consistent with an independent literature that treats mobility and loading as regulated rather than automatic.

experimental_context.tissue: Arabidopsis source and recipient tissues

limitations: The independent study supports regulated movement but not the same microtubule mechanism.
The mechanism should not be generalized across tissues or species without source-restricted and recipient-loading tests.

claim: Across the public record, the research framework evolved from broad genetic requirements to biochemical substrate protection, branched turnover, plural action modes, and spatial loading/movement gates; this is an agent synthesis rather than a verbatim personal statement.

experimental_context.tissue: multiple Arabidopsis tissues and biochemical systems

limitations: This is a cross-paper synthesis, not a quote or claim about Chen's current private views.
Multi-author papers are team results and do not imply individual endorsement of every formulation.

limitations: Only the three listed source records are covered by this card; it must not be generalized to the full corpus.
Bibliographic status must be rechecked when the corpus is updated.
Absence of a correction flag does not validate every scientific interpretation.
